description: This dataset contains responses to a citizen perception survey on temporary pedestrianisation, the conversion of vehicular streets into pedestrian-only zones for set periods, with an R analysis script. It was published on Zenodo on 6 February 2026 by Yasmany García-Ramírez of the Universidad Técnica Particular de Loja. Respondents are pedestrians and visitors, permanent business owners and staff, temporary vendors and residents, with tailored questions; variables cover demographics, transport mode, experience ratings, support for permanent pedestrianisation, perceived pollution reduction, business and resident impacts, importance of ten infrastructure factors such as lighting, security, furniture, accessibility and green space, and preferred days and times. Coverage: one pedestrianised area, whose city is not named in the record excerpt read. Access: Zenodo, one spreadsheet with Spanish headers and English translations. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: an exploratory case study; structural blanks reflect question branching. Simulation uses: evaluating street-to-plaza conversions and public space programming from user perspectives. Related records: the Lisbon temporary public space occupations dataset.
